questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to get a better-paid job
Why work makes people unhappy and how it could improve
The worst jobs the presenters have had
Why British workers are the happiest in Europe
questions.why: Beth asks how we can make sure our job doesn't make us unhappy, and that's what they discuss.

questions.q: What was difficult about Beth's job as a waitress?
options: Her boss was very unkind to the staff
The pay was very low for the long hours
She was on her feet ten hours a day
She had to work at night every weekend
questions.why: She says she was on her feet ten hours a day, and it was exhausting.

questions.q: According to Professor Damian Grimshaw, how does Britain compare with other European countries?
options: It scores badly on work intensity
British workers get many more holidays
British bosses give workers more freedom
British workers are paid much more money
questions.why: He says on surveys of 'work intensity', Britain scores really badly compared to European countries.

questions.q: What does Beth say makes a good job, apart from pay?
options: Having a friendly boss who listens to you
Working close to home so you can walk there
Having lots of targets to meet each week
Using your talents and some choice in how you work
questions.why: She says a good job uses your talents and gives you some choice over how and when you work.

questions.q: Why did many NHS nurses leave their jobs in 2022?
options: Because of low pay
Because of long, inflexible working hours
Because of injuries at work
Because they moved to other countries
questions.why: More than 15,000 nurses left, many because of the long and inflexible working hours.

questions.q: In Emma Stewart's trial, when could builders go home?
options: When the last person left the site
At seven in the evening
After they had worked eight hours
When they had finished their tasks well
questions.why: She says when you've done your tasks, and done them well, you can go home, with the same pay.

questions.q: What was a result of the task-based trial?
options: Projects were finished late and over budget
Workers were paid less for the same work
Work-life balance scores doubled
Workers did a lot more overtime each week
questions.why: Emma says work-life balance scores doubled and overtime went down.

questions.q: Why does Emma call the new way of working 'a win-win'?
options: It helps both the company and the workers
It helps workers but costs companies more
It is only good for the managers
It means builders can win prizes
questions.why: Projects were on time and on budget, and workers had better work-life balance.
